home.hero.pill: Open source · Works offline · 5 Indian languages
home.hero.title: No woman lost between screening and care.
home.hero.lead: FEMOS connects frontline health workers, the devices they already carry, doctors and government health systems, offline and in her language. AI agents do the paperwork. People make the decisions.
home.stat.errors: record errors caught before they reach a doctor
home.stat.agents: AI agents working alongside every health worker
home.stat.lead: median early warning before haemoglobin turns severe
home.stat.langs: Indian languages and 3 scripts, at every level
home.how.title: From her doorstep to the doctor, and back.
home.how.1.d: Any health worker, or the woman herself, records her history in any of five languages. A photo of the meter becomes a verified reading. FEMOS drafts; the worker confirms.
home.how.2.d: The doctor sees a priority queue and a one-page summary where every line links to its source and every warning cites WHO or national guidance. One click to refer.
home.how.3.d: Agents track every referral, propose escalations and draft discreet reminders in her language. Records flow to FHIR, OpenSRP and DHIS2 automatically.
home.feat.title: AI agents handle the paperwork. People make the decisions, faster.
home.feat.1.d: Intake, checks, handoff, follow-up, interoperability and supervision. They propose; a person approves.
home.feat.2.d: Unit mix-ups, decimal slips, contradictions, duplicates across scripts and reused photos, flagged before they reach a record.
home.feat.3.d: Capture, checks and handoff run on the phone. Everything syncs safely when there is a signal.
home.feat.4.d: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil and English, in native script, romanised or mixed. Her original words always stay with the record.
home.feat.5.d: One record per woman across every visit reveals falling haemoglobin, stalled referrals and school-level spikes early.
home.feat.6.d: Neutral messages, guardian consent for adolescents, photos that stay on the device, and an audit trail for every action.
home.lang.title: The same app, in the language she speaks.
home.lang.lead: Every screen, question, summary and message, in five languages. A case recorded in Tamil reads correctly for a doctor who reads Bengali.
home.ed.title: See the decline before it becomes an emergency.
home.ed.lead: FEMOS follows each woman across home visits, school camps and clinics. Its learning module spots patterns no single visit shows, and brings them to the right person early.
home.ed.2: Anaemia rising in a school or village
home.ed.4: A device model producing unreadable screens
home.kit.title: Works with the devices clinics already use.
home.kit.lead: Haemoglobin meters, BP monitors, glucometers and lab reports, read by camera, Bluetooth, lab file or double-checked entry. The FEMOS Kit adds a phone app and a one-page setup card.
team.title: The people behind FEMOS.
team.lead: Technology leadership from Empathy AI, with practising doctors who serve communities in and around Kolkata.
home.final.title: See FEMOS working.
home.final.lead: Open the field app on your phone, or the clinician console on your laptop. Sample cases are loaded.
footer.disclaimer: FEMOS is open-source software for women’s health, developed by Empathy AI Pvt Ltd with clinical and field partners in West Bengal. The public demo runs on sample records.
